message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 170, "amount_cents": 17127}, {"order_id": 175, "amount_cents": 2957}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund records myself rather than rely only on W2's handoff message. Starting with the orders.
The orders list is in, but I still need the refund records to check W2's claim that refunds were applied. I'll pull the refunds next.
The refund records match W2's handoff: orders 170 (acme) and 175 (cobalt) were refunded for 17127 and 2957. Next I'll get acme's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
acme's net_balance of 11259 matches my own check (23222 + 5164 - 17127 = 11259), and the refund records confirm the figure, so I'll record acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, which has orders 171 and 174 and no refunds, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance.
Birch's net_balance of 18633 matches my own check (11886 + 6747 = 18633, with no refunds on record), so I'll record its payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, with orders 172 and 175 and a refund of 2957 on order 175. I'll get its net balance from net_balance before recording anything.
Cobalt's net_balance of 62037 matches my own check (27875 + 37119 - 2957 = 62037), so I'll record its payout.
All three customers in the batch (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid. Each net_balance matched my own check against the orders and refunds, and every record_payout returned ok.
